approaches.name: national digital forest information, traceability and MRV systems
approaches.description: The project deploys and upgrades digital forest information, timber traceability and MRV systems to verify legality, monitor carbon and biodiversity, and share data in real time. Practices: national wood traceability and legality verification systems; digital MRV for forest inventories and carbon data; geospatial tools for biodiversity and forest status monitoring; Piloted satellite connectivity and digital MRV for forest monitoring; Digital NTFP statistics application for data collection and monitoring; SIGIF 2.0 forest information system with real-time data sharing; Third multi-resource National Forest Inventory with MRV software; Forest Information and Management System for coverage assessment; SIVL digital timber legality and traceability system modules; National forest inventory, monitoring system and forest cadaster; Earth observation, data analytics and AI for regional forest and biodiversity monitoring; SIGIF 2.0 and SIVL timber traceability systems for legality verification; Forest Information System for carbon stock and deforestation monitoring in CAR.
approaches.why_innovative: New process: digital legality verification of timber entering markets - cue: 'traceability' | category Technological; adoption apply; judged in 2 round(s); context expanded; final check: digital core, in_use before 2019

evidence.text: Subcomponent 1.2: Traceability, Certification, and Information Systems.

extra_evidence.text: National traceability and legality verification systems will be improved to facilitate the entry of legally sourced timber into domestic and export markets and to update forest inventories for more accurate management planning.

Financial support will be allocated for (i) hardware, software, and technical expertise for the development of forest inventories and data on forest carbon, where feasible, using digital Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV); and (ii) improved traceability and legality verification systems, including equipment, connectivity, hardware, software, training, and support for SMEs.

Investments will be aligned with the needs identified in each management plan and may encompass habitat restoration, biodiversity and forest status monitoring using geospatial tools and community engagement;
(ii) pilot and scale appropriate modern IT equipment and associated products and services (including satellite connectivity, digital MRV).
The Project will also develop a digital application for managing statistical data on NTFPs.
The proposed platform will enable efficient data collection, analysis, monitoring, and dissemination, improving transparency and decision-making.

(ii) establishing a professional organization for NTFP promotion, with dedicated staff and technological infrastructure; and (iii) provision of IT infrastructure and software for database management on NTFPs and wood energy.

Modernization of information systems to improve accuracy and granularity in forest coverage assessment and the quality of management planning for forests and protected areas through: 46Source: Awono, A., et.al.

(b) Support for the development of the third multi-resource National Forest Inventory (US$6.00 million equivalent IDA), through the procurement of qualified consultants, equipment, training and software, to increase the quality of MRV data, enable access to carbon markets and effective monitoring of forests and biodiversity, and to assess the current condition and potential of Cameroon’s forests and biodiversity and help plan future timber harvests.
Subcomponent 1.2: Traceability, Certification, Information Systems (US$3.25 million equivalent IDA): (a) This subcomponent will finance the development of a Forest Information and Management System.

This will include (i) preparation of a needs assessment, a tailored technical design, selection and deployment of software tools to improve accuracy and granularity in forest coverage assessments and management planning;
Subcomponent 1.2: Traceability, Certification, Information Systems (US$13.00 million equivalent IDA).

(a) Support to the National Legality and Verification System (Système Informatique de Vérification de Légalité, SIVL), including through (i) the development of additional modules to enhance timber traceability, and (ii) providing technical assistance to the MEF for forest legality and traceability coordination.

(b) Support for a national forest inventory, establishing a forest monitoring system and a forest cadaster and mapping of conservation and protection zones in the forest management units, and provision of technical equipment for these activities.

(iii) promotion of community forestry and multi-stakeholder participation in protected areas management;53 and, (iv) learning from regional and global expertise including to leverage advances in earth observation, communication, data analytics and Artificial Intelligence).54 (c) Partnerships will be established for training and knowledge sharing with the World Bank’s technology initiatives and with international programs in other parts of the world such as the Amazon.55 3.

The Program will support implementation of key objectives of the upcoming COMIFAC Convergence Plan (2026-2035) through technical assistance and knowledge sharing with member countries for (i) conservation and sustainable use of biological diversity;

Traceability, Certification, Information Systems Traceability Tools (Cameroon and RoC): By enhancing timber legality and traceability, the SIGIF 2.0 and SIVL, respectively, will help curb illegal logging, promote legal and sustainable forest management practices, reduce emissions from deforestation, and provide traceability data for national climate reporting systems.

Forest Information System (CAR): The development of the Forest Information System will enable better monitoring of forest carbon stocks, deforestation trends, and sustainable resource use and enhance decision-making for land-use planning, forest resilience, and biodiversity conservation through improved data collection, analysis, and accessibility.
